s: By what name was Pingali Venkayya, born in 1876 at Bhatlapenumarru, popularly known?
x: Pingali Venkayya, born in 1876 at Bhatlapenumarru, is popularly known as Jhanda Venkayya.

s: When was the National Flag of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
x: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag on 22 July 1947.

s: At which AICC session did Pingali Venkayya show his 1921 tricolour design to Gandhi?
x: Venkayya presented the design at the Bezwada AICC session; Gandhi added the charkha, later replaced by the Ashoka Chakra.

s:
Consider the following statements about Vande Mataram:
1. It was composed in 1875.
2. It appeared in Anandamath in 1882.
3. It was first sung at an INC session before it appeared in Anandamath.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Vande Mataram was composed in 1875 and appeared in Anandamath in 1882; Tagore first sang it at the INC session only in 1896.

s: When were the National Anthem and the National Song adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
x: Both were adopted on 24 January 1950; the National Flag was adopted on 22 July 1947.

s: At which session of the Indian National Congress was Jana Gana Mana first sung?
x: Jana Gana Mana was first sung at the Calcutta session of the INC on 27 December 1911.

s: Which symbol replaced the charkha on the National Flag adopted on 22 July 1947?
o: Dharma Chakra of Sarnath with lions
x: When the Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag on 22 July 1947, the Ashoka Chakra replaced the charkha.

s: Who first sang Vande Mataram at a session of the Indian National Congress in 1896?
x: Vande Mataram, written by Bankim Chandra Chatterji, was first sung at the 1896 INC session by Rabindranath Tagore.

s: Jana Gana Mana, the National Anthem, is the first of five stanzas of which kind of composition by Tagore?
x: Jana Gana Mana is the first of five stanzas of a Bengali Brahmo hymn by Tagore.

s: Pingali Venkayya was inspired after attending the 1906 INC session presided over by whom?
x: Pingali Venkayya attended the 1906 Calcutta session under Dadabhai Naoroji, which inspired him.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to the Constituent Assembly?
x: B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser; H.C. Mukherjee was Vice-President and B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

s: Who was the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly at its first sitting?
x: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha presided as temporary President; Rajendra Prasad became permanent President.

s:
Consider the following statements about the first session of the Constituent Assembly:
1. Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.
2. H.C. Mukherjee was a Vice-President.
3. The Muslim League attended the first sitting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Prasad was elected on 11 December 1946 and H.C. Mukherjee was Vice-President; the Muslim League boycotted the first sitting.

s: The Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly, B.N. Rau, later became a judge of which body?
x: B.N. Rau, Constitutional Adviser to the Assembly, later became a judge of the International Court of Justice.

s: Who chaired the Union Powers Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
x: Nehru chaired the Union Powers, Union Constitution and States Committees; Patel chaired the Advisory and Provincial Constitution Committees.

s: Who chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
x: Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution and Advisory Committees; Nehru chaired the Union Powers Committee.

s: Which of the following pairs of Constituent Assembly committees and chairmen is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Rules of Procedure Committee – Rajendra Prasad
x: The Steering Committee was chaired by Rajendra Prasad, not Nehru.

s: Who chaired the House Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
x: B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya of the Andhra region chaired the House Committee.

s: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
x: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee; B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser.

s: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted?
x: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

s: How long did the Constituent Assembly take to frame the Constitution?
x: It took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days, over 11 sessions.

s: How many sessions did the Constituent Assembly hold to frame the Constitution?
x: The Constitution was framed in 11 sessions.

s: Why was 26 January chosen as the date of commencement of the Constitution?
o: The day the Objectives Resolution was adopted
The anniversary of the first sitting
Purna Swaraj Day, set by the Lahore Congress
The day the Constitution was signed
x: The Lahore Congress (1929) had set 26 January 1930 as the day of complete independence (Purna Swaraj Day).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas)?
o: It was earlier observed as National Law Day
It marks the day the Constitution came into force
x: Constitution Day (26 November) marks the adoption of the Constitution; it came into force on 26 January 1950.

s: On which date did the members of the Constituent Assembly sign the Constitution at its last meeting?
x: The last meeting of the Constituent Assembly was on 24 January 1950, when members signed the Constitution.

s: In which year was the demand for a Constituent Assembly accepted in principle in the August Offer?
x: The demand was accepted in principle in the August Offer of 1940.

s: In 1938, on what basis did Nehru demand that the Assembly framing the constitution be elected?
x: In 1938 Nehru called for a constitution made by an Assembly elected on adult franchise.

s: Who among the following first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934?
x: M.N. Roy first proposed a Constituent Assembly in 1934; the Congress made it an official demand only in 1935.

s: In which year did the demand for a Constituent Assembly become an official demand of the Indian National Congress?
x: M.N. Roy raised the idea in 1934 and the INC adopted it as an official demand in 1935.

s: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the demand for a Constituent Assembly officially stated in 1936?
x:
Most books and keys: Faizpur (Dec 1936). Spectrum Modern India p.644 also records the Lucknow session (April 1936) rejecting any constitution imposed from outside.
The Congress restated its Constituent Assembly demand at the Faizpur session (December 1936); the Lucknow session earlier that year also rejected an imposed constitution. Haripura (1938) and Tripuri (1939) came later.

s: With which early document of 1895, sometimes credited to Tilak, is the first idea of a constitution for India linked?
x: The Swaraj Bill of 1895 was an early idea of a constitution for India; some sources credit Tilak.

s: Under which plan was the Constituent Assembly of India set up in 1946?
x: The Constituent Assembly was set up in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan.

s: Under the Cabinet Mission scheme, how were the provincial members of the Constituent Assembly elected?
o: Proportional representation by single transferable vote
x: Each community's members in the provincial assembly elected its representatives by PR-STV, with seats divided broadly by population.

s: Which two prominent leaders were NOT members of the Constituent Assembly?
x: Nearly every leader was a member except Gandhi and Jinnah. Nehru, Patel, Prasad, Ambedkar, Sarojini Naidu and Hansa Mehta were all members.

s: Why did the strength of the Constituent Assembly fall from 389 to 299?
o: withdrawal of Muslim League members from areas that went to Pakistan
x: After Partition, Muslim League members from territories that became part of Pakistan withdrew, reducing the strength from 389 to 299.

s: How many women were members of the Constituent Assembly?
x: The Constituent Assembly had 15 women members, such as Durgabai Deshmukh, Sarojini Naidu and Hansa Mehta.

s: Under the Cabinet Mission scheme, how were the representatives of the princely states chosen?
x: Princely states' members were to be nominated by the rulers; only provincial members were elected by STV.

s: In which context did Vallabhbhai Patel remark, "The British element is gone, but they have left mischief behind"?
o: the appointment of the Drafting Committee
x: Patel made the remark while discussing the legacy of separate electorates introduced during British rule.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly after the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. It became a fully sovereign body.
2. As the Dominion Legislature it was chaired by Rajendra Prasad, and as the constitution-making body by Mavalankar.
3. It continued as the Provisional Parliament till 1952.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct: the Act made it fully sovereign. Statement 2 is wrong: the roles are reversed - Prasad chaired the constitution-making body, Mavalankar the Dominion Legislature. Statement 3 is correct. So '1 and 2 only', '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' are wrong; answer is 1 and 3 only.

s: Who chaired the Constituent Assembly when it met as the Dominion Legislature?
x: G.V. Mavalankar chaired it as the Dominion Legislature; Rajendra Prasad chaired it as the constitution-making body.

s: Which party's National Executive demanded in 1946 that the Constituent Assembly be dissolved and re-elected by universal adult suffrage?
x: The Socialist Party, led by Jayaprakash Narayan and Ram Manohar Lohia, demanded dissolution and re-election by adult suffrage.

s: Why was the Constituent Assembly criticised as not being representative of the people?
o: Its members were indirectly elected under the restricted franchise of the 1935 Act
It was dominated by the Muslim League
Its members were nominated by the Governor-General
x: Its members were elected indirectly by provincial assemblies chosen on the limited 1935 Act franchise, not by adult franchise.

s: How many members attended the first sitting of the Constituent Assembly?
x:
Most books and keys: 211 members attended the first sitting (NextGen Polity 08 p.1). Strictly: Laxmikanth 8th ed. ch.2 p.40 gives 207.
The first sitting on 9 December 1946 was attended by 211 members (the usual figure); the Muslim League boycotted it. 284 signed the Constitution, 299 was the post-Partition strength and 389 the original.

s: When was the first sitting of the Constituent Assembly held?
x: The first sitting was on 9 December 1946; Prasad was elected on 11 December and the Objectives Resolution moved on 13 December.

s: On which date did Jawaharlal Nehru move the Objectives Resolution?
x: Nehru moved it on 13 December 1946; it was adopted on 22 January 1947.

s: On which date did the Constituent Assembly adopt the Objectives Resolution?
x: It was moved on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Objectives Resolution:
1. It was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru.
2. Its ideals became the basis of the Preamble.
3. It was adopted on the day it was moved.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Nehru moved it and its ideals shaped the Preamble; it was moved on 13 December 1946 but adopted only on 22 January 1947.

s: On which date did Jawaharlal Nehru accept the Andhra demand in the Constituent Assembly?
x: Nehru accepted it on 27 November 1947; Andhra was dropped from the Draft Constitution on 21 February 1948 and the Dhar Commission named on 17 June 1948.

s: Which member of the Constituent Assembly founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha?
x: Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha; Pattabhi Sitaramayya chaired the House Committee and Ranga was a peasant leader.

s: Which Constituent Assembly member from the Andhra region later became Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
x: M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar pressed for an independent judiciary and later became Deputy Speaker and Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

s: Which peasant leader from the Andhra region spoke in the Constituent Assembly on decentralisation, bicameralism and an Andhra Province?
x: N.G. Ranga, a peasant leader, spoke on decentralisation, emergency powers, bicameralism and an Andhra Province.

s: At which session was B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya President of the INC in 1948?
x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the 1948 Jaipur session of the INC.

s: China's construction of a road through which area was one of the causes of the India-China war of 1962?
x: China's road through Aksai Chin, with the McMahon Line dispute, the Dalai Lama's asylum and the Forward Policy, led to the 1962 war.

s: When did China declare a unilateral ceasefire in the 1962 war?
x: China declared a unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962; India's National Emergency was declared on 26 October 1962.

s: When was Goa liberated through Operation Vijay?
x: Goa was liberated in December 1961, after the Dalai Lama's flight (1959) and Chou En-lai's visit (1960).

s: Which Defence Minister resigned in the aftermath of the 1962 India-China war?
x: V.K. Krishna Menon resigned after the 1962 war; an Emergency was proclaimed on 26 October 1962.

s: When did the Dalai Lama flee to India?
x: The Dalai Lama fled in March 1959, before Chou En-lai's visit (April 1960) and Goa's liberation (December 1961).

s: On which date was a National Emergency proclaimed during the India-China war of 1962?
x: The Emergency was proclaimed on 26 October 1962; China declared a unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962.

s: Where was Jawaharlal Nehru imprisoned when he wrote "The Discovery of India"?
x: The Discovery of India was written in Ahmednagar Fort jail. Yerwada is linked with Gandhi and the Poona Pact, Mandalay with Tilak's imprisonment, and the Cellular Jail with revolutionaries such as Savarkar.

s: Who said, "Everything else can wait, but not agriculture"?
x: The remark is Jawaharlal Nehru's. Gandhi, Ambedkar and Mahalanobis are not credited with it; Mahalanobis is in fact associated with the industry-first Second Plan.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gandhi favoured a decentralised village and cottage-industry economy.
2. Nehru favoured heavy industry, science and central planning.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Gandhi emphasised decentralised villages and cottage industries, whereas Nehru supported heavy industry, science and central planning.

s: Jawaharlal Nehru represented which constituency in the Lok Sabha?
x: Nehru's seat was Phulpur.

s: Which of the following was an influence on Jawaharlal Nehru?
x: Nehru was influenced by Fabian socialism, British liberalism, Gandhi and Soviet planning; German nationalism was not an influence.

s: Who is the author of 'Glimpses of World History'?
x: Glimpses of World History is one of Nehru's books, along with The Discovery of India.

s: Who among the following edited 'A Bunch of Old Letters' (1958)?
x: A Bunch of Old Letters (1958) is a collection of letters edited by Jawaharlal Nehru.

s: On which date did Jawaharlal Nehru die in office as Prime Minister?
x: Nehru was Prime Minister from 15 August 1947 till his death on 27 May 1964.

s: Who said, 'Everything could wait but not agriculture'?
x: Nehru said 'Everything could wait but not agriculture' after Independence.

s: How was the Planning Commission set up on 15 March 1950?
x: It was set up by an executive resolution and was replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015.

s: Who was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first Deputy Chairman; Nehru, as Prime Minister, was the ex officio Chairman and M.S. Ahluwalia the last Deputy Chairman.

s: When was the National Development Council set up?
x: The NDC was set up on 6 August 1952, chaired by the PM, and gave final approval to Five Year Plans.

s: Which body gave final approval to the Five Year Plans?
x: The NDC (1952), chaired by the PM, gave final approval to the Plans.

s: Who was the last Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
x: The first Deputy Chairman was Gulzarilal Nanda and the last was M.S. Ahluwalia.

s: Which body replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015?
x: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

s: Who was appointed Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog in May 2026?
x: In May 2026, Ashok Kumar Lahiri was appointed Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog.

s: What was a major consequence of the strategy of the Second Five Year Plan?
o: Food shortages and inflation following the neglect of agriculture
Immediate food self-sufficiency and price stability
The replacement of central planning by annual plans
x: The Second Plan's emphasis on heavy industry neglected agriculture, contributing to food shortages and inflation.

s: By what name was the Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) known?
x: The Third Plan was the 'Gadgil Yojana', based on the Sandy-Chakravarty model; it was derailed by the 1962 and 1965 wars and drought.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Second Five Year Plan – Harrod-Domar model
First Five Year Plan – Mahalanobis model
Third Five Year Plan – Gadgil Yojana
Second Five Year Plan – Gadgil Yojana
x: The Third Plan was called the Gadgil Yojana; the First Plan used the Harrod-Domar model and the Second the Mahalanobis model.

s: After the failure of the Third Five Year Plan, during which period was the 'Plan Holiday' with three annual plans?
x: The Third Plan's failure led to the Plan Holiday of 1966–69, with three annual plans and a devaluation of the rupee.

s: To which sector did the Mahalanobis strategy give primary emphasis?
x: The Mahalanobis strategy stressed industrial development and was criticised for neglecting agriculture.

s: On which model was the First Five Year Plan (1951-56) based?
x: The First Plan followed the Harrod-Domar model; the Second followed Mahalanobis.

s: What growth rate did the First Five Year Plan (1951-56) achieve against its target of 2.1%?
x: The First Plan, based on the Harrod-Domar model, achieved 3.6% growth against a target of 2.1%.

s: On which model was the Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) based?
x: The Third Plan, also called the Gadgil Yojana, was based on the Sandy-Chakravarty model.

s: Under the UGC Act of which year did the UGC, set up in 1953, become a statutory body?
x: The UGC became statutory under the UGC Act, 1956; it is not a constitutional body.

s: Under whose leadership was the Atomic Energy Commission established in 1948?
x: The Atomic Energy Commission was established in 1948 under Homi J. Bhabha.

s:
Consider the following statements about Rabindra Bharati, Hyderabad:
1. It was built to commemorate the birth centenary of Rabindranath Tagore.
2. It was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru on 11 October 1961.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Rabindra Bharati, Hyderabad, was built for Tagore's birth centenary and was inaugurated by Nehru on 11 October 1961.

s: In which year was the first IIT set up at Kharagpur?
x: The first IIT, at Kharagpur, was set up in 1951.

s: In which year was AIIMS, New Delhi, established?
x: AIIMS New Delhi was set up in 1956.

s: In which year was the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) set up?
x: CSIR was set up in 1942; its laboratories grew under Nehru.

s: Who sponsored the Bandung Conference of 1955?
x: The Colombo Powers (India, Indonesia, Burma, Ceylon, Pakistan) sponsored Bandung, where Panchsheel was absorbed into the Ten Principles.

s: Which was the first country outside India and China to adopt Panchsheel (1954)?
x: Burma was the first country outside the India-China pair to adopt Panchsheel in 1954, not Indonesia.

s:
Consider the following statements about the principles of Panchsheel:
1. Non-aggression is one of its principles.
2. Collective military defence against power blocs is one of its principles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Non-aggression is one of the five Panchsheel principles; collective military defence against power blocs was not.

s: Where was the Non-Aligned Movement formally established in 1961?
x: The Non-Aligned Movement was formalised in 1961 at Belgrade.

s: Who headed the Neutral Nations Repatriation Commission in Korea (1953), chaired by India?
x: India chaired the Commission in Korea in 1953 under Gen. K.S. Thimayya.

s: During the Suez crisis of 1956, Nehru condemned the attack on Egypt by which countries?
x: Nehru condemned the Anglo-French-Israeli attack on Egypt in 1956.

s: In 1954, Nehru and Zhou Enlai signed Panchsheel as part of an agreement on what?
x: Panchsheel (29 April 1954) formed part of the India-China agreement on trade with Tibet.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Bandung Conference
2. Panchsheel Agreement
3. Belgrade Conference of the Non-Aligned Movement
4. Flight of the Dalai Lama to India
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Panchsheel was signed in April 1954, Bandung met in 1955, the Dalai Lama fled in March 1959 and NAM met at Belgrade in 1961.

s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, how many industries were reserved for the State in Schedule A?
x: Schedule A reserved 17 industries for the State; Schedule B had 12.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956:
1. Schedule B listed 12 industries in which the State would increasingly set up units.
2. Schedule C was reserved for the public sector.
3. Schedule A listed 17 industries reserved for the State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Schedules A (17) and B (12) are correct; Schedule C was left to the private sector.

s: The Industrial Policy Resolution of which year laid down the first framework for the roles of the public and private sectors?
x: The 1948 Resolution gave the first framework; the 1956 Resolution created Schedules A, B and C.

s: In what way does the Indian State differ from the Western model of strict separation of religion and State?
o: May intervene to reform certain social practices
x: India has no State religion and stays neutral, but unlike the Western model it permits State intervention for social reform.

s: In which year was the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act enacted?
x: It was enacted in 1956, the same year as the Hindu Succession and Minority and Guardianship Acts; the Hindu Marriage Act was 1955.

s: Which Article of the Constitution protects the educational institutions of minorities?
x: Article 30 protects the rights of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.

s: Article 343 made Hindi in Devanagari script the official language. For how long did it allow English to continue?
x: Article 343 made Hindi in the Devanagari script the official language and provided for the use of English for 15 years.

s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resigned from the Union Cabinet in 1951 primarily because which proposal was stalled and diluted?
x: Ambedkar resigned in 1951, on 27 September, when the Hindu Code Bill dealing with women’s rights in inheritance, marriage and divorce was stalled and diluted.

s: Which post did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar hold in Jawaharlal Nehru's first cabinet of independent India (1947)?
x: Ambedkar was free India's first Law Minister in Nehru's 1947 cabinet and resigned in 1951 over the Hindu Code Bill. He had been Labour Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council (1942-46), before independence; he was not Home or Education Minister.

s: Which of the Hindu Code Acts was enacted in 1955?
x: The Hindu Marriage Act came in 1955; the other three Acts in 1956.

s: What cabinet ratio between Andhra and Telangana did the Gentlemen's Agreement provide for?
x: It provided a 60:40 cabinet ratio, a Telangana Regional Committee, protection of surplus funds and job/education safeguards.

s: As Chief Minister of Andhra State, Bezawada Gopala Reddy represented Andhra in which agreement?
x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy represented Andhra in the Gentlemen's Agreement of 20 February 1956 with Telangana leaders.

s:
Consider the following statements about the legislature of the first Andhra State:
1. It had a Legislative Council.
2. Its Assembly consisted of members elected to the Madras Assembly in 1952.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The Andhra Assembly consisted of members elected to the Madras Assembly in 1952, and Andhra State had no Legislative Council.

s: Who inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Andhra State at Kurnool.

s: Which of the following pairs about the final Bellary adjustments is correctly matched?
x: On Justice Mishra's report, Bellary taluk went to Mysore, Rayadurg to Anantapur, and Adoni and Alur to Kurnool.

s: Who was the first Chief Justice of the High Court of Andhra State at Guntur?
x: Koka Subba Rao was the first Chief Justice of the Andhra High Court, set up at Guntur in 1954.

s: At its formation in 1953, Andhra State had how many districts?
x: Andhra State had 11 districts: 7 in Coastal Andhra and 4 in Rayalaseema.

s: Which one of the following was NOT included among the districts of Andhra State at the time of its formation?
x: Vizianagaram district did not exist at the time of Andhra State formation. Nellore, Kurnool and Chittoor were included.

s: In the Madras Assembly vote on the capital of Andhra State, by what margin did Kurnool defeat Vijayawada?
x: Kurnool won 79 to 53, helped by five non-Andhra votes; Prakasam did not vote.

s: The 1955 mid-term election in Andhra State followed the fall of whose ministry?
x: It followed the fall of Prakasam's ministry; the United Congress front (Congress, Krishikar Lok Party, PSP) contested against the Communists.

s: On which date was the High Court of Andhra State at Guntur set up?
x: It was set up on 5 July 1954; until then the Madras High Court served Andhra State.

s: In which year did the Andhra Pradesh Legislature become bicameral for the first time?
x: The Legislative Council was created in 1958, making the legislature bicameral.

s: Who was the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State?
x: B. Ramakrishna Rao became the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State in 1952. Prakasam and Gopala Reddy headed Andhra State, and Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Speaker of Andhra State – Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
First Chief Minister of Andhra State – Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
First Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh – Tanguturi Prakasam
First Governor of Andhra Pradesh – Chandulal Madhavlal Trivedi
x: Chandulal Madhavlal Trivedi was the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh. Prakasam was the first CM of Andhra State, Sanjiva Reddy the first CM of Andhra Pradesh and Nallapati Venkatramaiah the first Speaker of Andhra State.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: First Speaker of Andhra State – Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao
First Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh – K.V. Rangareddy
First Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra State – K.V. Rangareddy
First Speaker of the AP Legislative Assembly – Nallapati Venkatramaiah
x: K.V. Rangareddy was the first Deputy CM of Andhra Pradesh. Nallapati Venkatramaiah was the first Speaker of Andhra State, Kaleswara Rao the first Speaker of the AP Assembly and N. Sanjeeva Reddy the first Deputy CM of Andhra State.

s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State?
x: T. Prakasam became CM on 1 October 1953; Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the last.

s: Over which issue did Prakasam's ministry fall on 15 November 1954 after a no-confidence vote?
x: It fell over the prohibition row, leading to President's rule till 28 March 1955.

s: In the 1955 mid-term election in Andhra State, the Congress won how many seats?
x: The Congress won 119 seats and the CPI 15; Bezawada Gopala Reddy became CM.

s: In the 1955 mid-term poll, which party joined the Congress and the PSP in the United Congress front?
x: The front of Congress, Krishikar Lok Party and PSP fought the Communists.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched for Andhra State (1953-56)?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court – Koka Subba Rao
x: C.M. Trivedi was the only Governor of Andhra State; Bhimsen Sachar was the second Governor of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Which site did the Communists led by P. Sundarayya favour in the capital debate?
x: The Communists led by P. Sundarayya backed Vijayawada/Guntur as the capital. The Praja Socialist Party (not the Krishikar Lok Party) backed Tirupati, and the Congress backed Kurnool.

s: On which date did the Andhra State Bill receive assent?
x: Introduced on 10 August 1953, the Bill received assent on 14 September 1953, and Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953.

s: Which of the following pairs (proposed capital site – supporter) is correctly matched?
x: Vijayawada/Guntur was backed by the Communists (P. Sundarayya); Kurnool by Congress, Prakasam's group and Rayalaseema leaders; and Tirupati by the Praja Socialist Party, not the Krishikar Lok Party.

s: Which was the first linguistic state of India, formed on 1 October 1953?
x: Andhra State, carved out of Madras State on 1 October 1953, was the first state formed on a linguistic basis.

s: For which financial year did Bezawada Gopala Reddy present the budget of Andhra State?
x: Bezawada Gopala Reddy presented the Andhra State budget for 1955-56.

s: Which office in Andhra State (1953) was first held by Nallapati Venkatramaiah?
o: Chief Justice of the High Court
x: Nallapati Venkatramaiah was the first Speaker of the Andhra State Assembly; C.M. Trivedi was Governor and Koka Subba Rao Chief Justice.

s: During which period was Bezawada Gopala Reddy the Chief Minister of Andhra State?
x: He became Chief Minister after the 1955 mid-term poll and was the last Chief Minister of Andhra State before Andhra Pradesh was formed in 1956.

s: Who succeeded C.M. Trivedi as Governor of Andhra Pradesh?
x: C.M. Trivedi was the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh; Bhimsen Sachar was the second.

s: Which party backed Tirupati as the capital of Andhra State?
x: The Praja Socialist Party backed Tirupati; the Communists wanted Vijayawada or Guntur and the Congress backed Kurnool.

s: Who was the first president of the Hyderabad State Congress?
x: Govinda Rao Nanal was the first president of the Hyderabad State Congress.

s: Who was the first Muslim of Hyderabad to join the Indian National Congress?
x: Mulla Abdul Qayyum was the first Hyderabad Muslim to join the INC.

s: Koka Subba Rao, the first Chief Justice of the High Court of Andhra State at Guntur, later held which office?
x: Koka Subba Rao was the first Chief Justice of the Andhra High Court (1954) and later Chief Justice of India (1966-67).

s: After Prakasam's ministry fell on 15 November 1954, till when did President's rule continue in Andhra State?
x: After the fall of Prakasam's ministry on 15 November 1954, President's rule lasted till 28 March 1955.

s: Who was the first Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly formed in 1956?
x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao was the first Speaker of Andhra Pradesh (1956); Nallapati Venkatramaiah was Speaker of Andhra State.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Sribagh Agreement was concluded on 16 November 1937.
The First Andhra Mahasabha was held in 1913 at Bapatla.
The Gentlemen's Agreement was concluded in 1937.
The First Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held on 28 January 1934 at Madras.
x: The Gentlemen's Agreement was concluded on 20 February 1956; the 1937 pact was the Sribagh Agreement.

s: Besides Fazal Ali, who were the members of the States Reorganisation Commission?
x: The SRC (announced 22 December 1953) had Fazal Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar.

s: On which date was the Gentlemen's Agreement between Andhra and Telangana leaders made?
x: The Gentlemen's Agreement is dated 20 February 1956; 16 November 1937 is the Sri Bagh Pact.

s: Which Chief Minister of Hyderabad State, earlier a supporter of a separate Telangana, later changed his stand to favour early merger of the Telugu areas?
x: B. Ramakrishna Rao, Hyderabad's first elected CM (1952), changed his stand and favoured early merger with Andhra (the year is given as 1954 or 1955 in different keys).

s: Who was the first Chief Minister of Andhra State (1953)?
x: T. Prakasam became the first Chief Minister of Andhra State in 1953.

s: What is the Youngmen's Literary Association at Guntur, founded in 1903, regarded as?
o: Venue of the Sri Bagh Pact
x: The Youngmen's Literary Association at Guntur in 1903 is regarded as the cradle of the Andhra movement.

s: Who moved the first formal separate-province resolution at the Nidadavolu conference of 1912?
x: Jonnavittula Gurunatham moved the first formal resolution for a separate province at Nidadavolu in 1912.

s: How did Guthi Kesava Pillai, at the Mahanandi meeting of April 1913, describe the demand for separation?
o: A movement led by the Madras Government
x: At Mahanandi in April 1913, Guthi Kesava Pillai considered separation impractical and called it a “Brahmin movement.”

s: Which of the following early Andhra movement events is NOT correctly matched with its year?
x: The Vizag district meeting was held in June 1913, not 1903; the other three are correctly dated.

s: After the Bapatla conference of 1913, which district meeting considered the separate Andhra demand 'not yet ripe'?
x: Nellore called the demand 'not yet ripe', while Guntur, Vijayawada, Godavari, Vizag and Chittoor backed it.

s: Who moved the early proposal for a separate Andhra province, which Nyapati Subba Rao opposed?
x: The proposal was moved by Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu; Krishna Rao moved the amendment and a committee under Pattabhi Sitaramayya followed.

s:
Consider the following statements about B.N. Sarma and the first Andhra Mahasabha:
1. He presided over the first Andhra Mahasabha.
2. He cautioned that the demand for a separate province might do more harm than good at that stage.
3. He held that a separate province was essential before any work for Andhra uplift could begin.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: B.N. Sarma presided at the first Mahasabha and warned that the separate-province demand might do more harm than good then; so statement 3 is wrong.

s: Who said, "First we are Indians, then we are Andhras"?
x: The statement expressed B.N. Sarma’s emphasis on Indian identity before regional identity.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Konda Venkatappayya — Moved the separate-province resolution
Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu — Moved the separate-province resolution
Unnava Lakshminarayana — Presided over the first session
x: Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu moved the separate-province resolution at Bapatla (1913). Konda Venkatappayya was the secretary and B.N. Sarma was the president there, so the other pairs are wrong.

s: Which of the following pairs about the early Andhra movement is correctly matched?
o: Bapatla, 1913 – First formal resolution for a separate province
Nidadavolu, 1912 – First formal resolution for a separate province
Nidadavolu, 1912 – First session called Andhra Mahasabha
x: Nidadavolu (1912) saw the first formal resolution; Bapatla (1913) was the first numbered Andhra Conference and Vijayawada (1914) the first session called Andhra Mahasabha.

s: Of which town was Manda Suryanarayana, who presided over the Vizag district meeting of June 1913, the municipal chairman?
x: Manda Suryanarayana was Vizianagaram's municipal chairman; Guntur's first was Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu. The meeting started the weekly Andhra Advocate.

s: The agenda of the Bapatla session of 1913 included lifting the ban on the entry of Telugus into which service?
x: The Bapatla agenda included removal of the ban on Telugus entering the Army, an English paper and a fund for technical training abroad.

s: Who presided over the Andhra Mahasabha Committee formed at Guntur in 1912-13?
x: Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu, Guntur's first municipal chairman, was its president.

s: Who was the secretary of the Nidadavolu joint conference of 1912?
x: Konda Venkatappayya was secretary; Gurunatham moved the province resolution there.

s: After the province resolution was deferred at Bapatla (1913), under whom was a committee formed to collect opinion?
x: On Krishna Rao's amendment to collect opinion, a committee under Pattabhi was formed; Nyapati Subba Rao and Mocherla had opposed the resolution.

s:
Consider the following statements about the first Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla, 1913:
1. A separate Telugu university was first demanded there.
2. The separate-province resolution was passed there.
3. Its agenda included a fund for technical training abroad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Bapatla first demanded a Telugu university and listed technical training abroad; the province resolution was deferred, and passed only at Vijayawada in 1914.

s: What did the joint conference of the Guntur, Krishna and Godavari districts held at Nidadavolu in 1912 do?
o: Opposed the formation of any linguistic province
Demanded a separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as capital
Passed the first formal resolution for a separate province
x: The Nidadavolu conference of 1912 passed the first formal resolution demanding a separate province. The resolution was moved by Gurunatham.

s: On which date was the first Andhra Mahasabha held at Bapatla?
x: The first Andhra Mahasabha met at Bapatla on 26 May 1913; 11 April 1914 was the Vijayawada session.

s: Who were the President and the Secretary, respectively, of the first Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla (1913)?
o: Nyapati Subba Rao and Konda Venkatappayya
B.N. Sarma and Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu
x: B.N. Sarma presided at Bapatla and Konda Venkatappayya was its secretary; Ramadasu Pantulu moved the province resolution.

s: Who started the weekly Andhra Advocate after the Vizag district meeting of June 1913?
x: Manda Suryanarayana, municipal chairman of Vizianagaram, presided over the Vizag district meeting and started the Andhra Advocate for propaganda.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra movement during 1913–1920:
1. It demanded an Andhra State and an Andhra University.
2. It opposed the use of Telugu in education and administration.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: This propaganda phase had four objectives: Andhra State, Andhra University, development of Telugu and cultural revival. It promoted Telugu rather than opposing it, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: In which year was the demand for a separate Andhra university first raised at the first session of the Andhra Mahasabha?
x: The university demand was first raised at the first session in 1913; Telugu as medium of instruction was demanded at the third session in 1915.

s: By what other name was Swami Sitaram, who undertook a fast for a separate Andhra State in 1951, known?
x: Swami Sitaram was the popular name of Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri, a Gandhian associated with the Andhra movement.

s: In which year was Nellore district renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District?
x: Nellore district was renamed Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District in 2008 by the government headed by Chief Minister Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.

s: How long did Swami Sitaram's fast for a separate Andhra State in 1951 last?
x: Swami Sitaram fasted for 35 days in 1951 for a separate Andhra State.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a demand associated with Swami Sitaram's 1951 fast?
o: Settlement of Madras city's status within three years
Immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra State
Formation of Andhra State by 2 October 1951
Neither Andhra nor Tamil interests controlling Madras city during the interim
x: The demands concerned the formation of Andhra State, settlement of Madras city's status, and an interim arrangement over the city. Merger of Telangana was not one of the stated demands.

s: By what margin did Sanjiva Reddy defeat N.G. Ranga in the April 1951 APCC election?
x: Sanjiva Reddy won by five votes, after which Prakasam and Ranga formed the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party.

s: To which community did Potti Sriramulu, born on 16 March 1901, belong?
x: Potti Sriramulu was born on 16 March 1901 in an Arya Vysya family. His ancestral village was Gajula Dinne in Nellore.

s: The earlier fasts of Potti Sriramulu were primarily undertaken for which cause?
o: Demand for prohibition in Madras Presidency
x: His earlier fasts were undertaken for Harijan causes, including temple entry and Harijan welfare. The 1952 fast was his only fast for statehood.

s:
Assertion (A): Potti Sriramulu's constructive work included khadi, prohibition and Harijan uplift.
Reason (R): Potti Sriramulu was born in Nellore town, his ancestral village.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: he was born in Madras, and his ancestral village was Gajula Dinne in Nellore district.

s: Potti Sriramulu's 29-day fast at Wardha in 1948 was associated with which combination?
o: Harijan Day and a grant of one crore rupees
Temple entry and the formation of Andhra State
Gandhi Smarak Din and the creation of Rayalaseema
Prohibition and the establishment of Andhra University
x: The Wardha fast in 1948 was associated with the observance of Harijan Day and a grant of one crore rupees. Madras also marked Harijan Welfare Day on the thirtieth of every month.

s: On 19 December 1952, from which areas did Jawaharlal Nehru announce that Andhra State would be formed?
o: Telangana and the coastal districts of Madras Presidency
The undisputed Telugu-speaking areas, excluding Madras city
All Telugu-speaking areas including Madras city
The entire Madras Presidency excluding Rayalaseema
x: Nehru announced that Andhra State would be formed from the undisputed Telugu areas, while Madras city would be excluded.

s: After Potti Sriramulu's death, riots and police firing broke out. How many persons died in the firing?
x: Sriramulu's death was followed by riots and police firing in which seven people died; Nehru then announced Andhra State in Parliament on 19 December 1952.

s: Which one of the following was NOT one of the three conditions associated with Potti Sriramulu's demand?
o: Madras city should become a Chief Commissioner's State by agreement
The Andhra State should include the whole of the Madras Presidency
The Centre should announce the formation of Andhra State immediately
x: The three conditions concerned immediate announcement, unity among Andhra leaders and making Madras a Chief Commissioner's State by agreement. Inclusion of the entire Madras Presidency was not a condition.

s: Which of the following is a title associated with Potti Sriramulu?
x: Potti Sriramulu is known by the title Amarajeevi, meaning Immortal Martyr. He is also associated with the title “Andhra Martyra Martanda.”

s: Which anniversary of Potti Sriramulu was marked by the unveiling of his 58-foot 'Statue of Sacrifice' at Amaravati on 16 March 2026?
x: Born 16 March 1901, Sriramulu's 125th birth anniversary fell on 16 March 2026, when CM Chandrababu Naidu unveiled the statue.

s: Potti Sriramulu sought the formation of a state comprising which of the following areas?
o: The Telugu-speaking districts along with the entire Madras city area
The Telugu-speaking districts of Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema
x: Potti Sriramulu demanded a separate state consisting of both Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema. The question of Madras city was left for later negotiation.

s: Potti Sriramulu spent about how many years at Sabarmati Ashram?
x: He spent about three years at Sabarmati Ashram (APPSC G2 2017).

s: On which date did Nehru announce in Parliament that Andhra State would be formed?
x: Nehru announced it on 19 December 1952, four days after Sriramulu's death on 15 December.

s: Gajula Dinne, the ancestral village of Potti Sriramulu, is in which district?
x: His ancestral village Gajula Dinne is in Nellore district; he was born in Madras.

s: After Sriramulu's 1948 Wardha fast, Madras observed Harijan Welfare Day on which day of every month?
x: Madras declared the 30th of every month Harijan Welfare Day.

s: Potti Sriramulu, honoured with the title 'Amarajeevi', died on the 58th day of his fast. On which date did he die?
x: Sriramulu began his fast on 19 October 1952 and died on its 58th day, 15 December 1952, earning the title 'Amarajeevi'. 19 December 1952 is the date of Nehru's announcement in Parliament (a common trap), and 1 October 1953 is the formation of Andhra State.

s: On Vinoba Bhave's appeal, which leader ended his 1951 fast for a separate Andhra State?
x: Swami Sitaram (Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri) ended his 35-day fast in 1951 on Vinoba Bhave's appeal.

s: Where did Swami Sitaram undertake his 35-day fast for a separate Andhra State in 1951?
x: Swami Sitaram fasted at Guntur from 15 August to 20 September 1951.

s: In whose house at Mylapore, Madras, did Potti Sriramulu undertake his fast unto death in 1952?
x: The fast began on 19 October 1952 and was held at Bulusu Sambamurthy's house in Mylapore.

s: Which leader began a fast unto death on 19 October 1952 for a separate Andhra State?
x: Potti Sriramulu began his fast on 19 October 1952 and died on its 58th day, 15 December 1952.

s: On which day of his fast did Potti Sriramulu die?
x: He died on the 58th day of his fast; 35 days was Swami Sitaram's fast and 29 days his own Wardha fast of 1948.

s: In which year was Potti Sriramulu born?
x: Potti Sriramulu was born on 16 March 1901 at Madras.

s: For what cause did Potti Sriramulu fast at the Venugopala Swamy temple, Nellore, in 1946?
o: Entry of Harijans into the temple
x: His 1946 fast at the Nellore Venugopala Swamy temple was for Harijan entry into the temple.

s: Which university in Andhra Pradesh is named after Potti Sriramulu?
x: Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University is named after him, along with Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District.

s: After Sanjiva Reddy beat N.G. Ranga in the APCC election of April 1951, which party did Prakasam and Ranga form?
x: After Ranga lost the April 1951 APCC poll by 5 votes, Prakasam and Ranga formed the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party.

s: At the Nellore session of 1917, 480 of the 740 delegates came from Nellore. How was voting therefore conducted?
x: Since 480 of the 740 delegates came from Nellore, voting was conducted district-wise to avoid domination by one district.

s: Where was the second Andhra Mahasabha session, which passed the resolution demanding a separate Andhra province, held?
x: The second session, held at Vijayawada on 11 April 1914, passed the resolution demanding a separate Andhra province.

s:
Consider the following statements about presidents of the Andhra Mahasabha sessions:
1. Nyapati Subba Rao presided over the second session.
2. Nemali Pattabhi Ramarao presided over the third session.
3. Mocherla Ramachandra Rao presided over the fourth session.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Nyapati Subba Rao presided over the second and Mocherla Ramachandra Rao over the fourth session; Nemali Pattabhi Ramarao presided over the sixth, not the third (Panuganti Ramarayaningar).

s: Where was the fourth Andhra Mahasabha session, which demanded a separate Andhra Congress circle, held?
x: The fourth session was held at Kakinada in May 1916 and demanded that the AICC create a separate Andhra Congress circle.

s: The special Andhra Sabha held at Guntur on 17 August 1918 protested that:
o: The Montagu-Chelmsford proposals did not provide for an Andhra province
The AICC had rejected Telugu as a medium of instruction
The Andhra Provincial Congress Conference had been dissolved
Madras city had been included in the Andhra province
x: The Guntur special session protested that the Montagu-Chelmsford proposals made no provision for an Andhra province.

s: Who presided over the fourth Andhra Mahasabha at Kakinada (1916) and was called the 'Gokhale of South India'?
x: Mocherla Ramachandra Rao, the 'Gokhale of South India', presided at Kakinada; a women's session was held there under Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi.

s:
Arrange the following Andhra Mahasabha sessions in chronological order:
A. Session at Kakinada
B. Session at Bapatla
C. Session at Kadapa
D. Session at Visakhapatnam
x: The sessions occurred at Bapatla in 1913, Visakhapatnam in 1915, Kakinada in 1916 and Kadapa in 1918.

s: Who led the Andhra delegation that met Edwin Montagu in Madras on 20 December 1917?
x: Nyapati Subba Rao led the delegation that met Montagu in Madras on 20 December 1917 to press for an Andhra province.

s: Where was the Andhra Mahasabha session of November 1941, presided over by Sir Vijayanand ('Sir Vijaya'), held?
x: He presided at Visakhapatnam in November 1941 and met Stafford Cripps on 2 April 1942.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Third Andhra Mahasabha?
o: It was held at Visakhapatnam in 1915.
It demanded a separate Andhra Province.
It was presided over by the Raja of Panagal.
x: The Third Andhra Mahasabha met at Visakhapatnam in 1915, not Bellary. It was presided over by the Raja of Panagal and demanded a separate Andhra Province.

s: Besides a separate Andhra Province, what did the Third Andhra Mahasabha (Visakhapatnam, 1915) demand?
o: Madras as the capital of Andhra
the mother tongue as the medium of instruction in secondary schools
x: The 1915 Visakhapatnam session demanded a separate Andhra Province (Andhra Rashtram) and the mother tongue as the medium in secondary schools.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Vijayanagar Gajapati presided over the 1936 Bellary convention. B.N. Sarma presided in 1913, Panuganti Ramarayaningar in 1915 and Nemali Pattabhirama Rao at the first Rayalaseema Mahasabha.

s: Who presided over the Silver Jubilee session of the Andhra Mahasabha at Vijayawada in 1937?
x: Kadapa Koti Reddy presided over the 1937 session (and the 1931 Special Andhra Sabha); H.M. Sitaram Reddy only inaugurated it.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Andhra Mahasabha convention met at Bellary in 1936. The first Rayalaseema Mahasabha met at Madras in 1934, the first Nizam Andhra Mahasabha at Jogipet in 1930, and the second Vishalandhra Mahasabha at Hyderabad in 1954.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 1936 Andhra Mahasabha convention:
1. It was held at Bellary.
2. It paved the way for the Gentlemen's Agreement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 1936 convention met at Bellary to bridge Coastal-Rayalaseema distrust and paved the way for the Sri Bagh Pact of 1937, not the Gentlemen's Agreement.

s: At the special Mahasabha at Guntur in 1918, what did Pattabhi Sitaramayya propose?
o: a deputation to the Round Table Conference
the transfer of Bellary to Madras
a boycott of the Simon Commission
x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya proposed an All-India Linguistic States Conference at the special Guntur Mahasabha.

s: At the 1937 Silver Jubilee session, in which matters did Rayalaseema leaders demand safeguards?
o: Separate army recruitment and the capital
Cabinet representation, irrigation and the capital
Cabinet representation and separate army recruitment
x: The 1937 safeguards concerned Cabinet representation, irrigation and the capital; separate army recruitment was not among them.

s: Where was the first session to be called the 'Andhra Mahasabha' held?
x: The second session at Vijayawada (11 April 1914) was the first to be called the Andhra Mahasabha.

s: Who moved the separate-province resolution passed at the Vijayawada session of 1914?
x: Manda Suryanarayana moved it at Vijayawada, presided over by Nyapati Subba Rao; Ramadasu Pantulu had moved it at Bapatla.

s: Which demand was rejected at the Nellore session of the Andhra Mahasabha in 1917?
o: Mother tongue as medium of instruction
x: The Nellore session (president Konda Venkatappayya) rejected the Madras city demand.

s: Who presided over the special Andhra Mahasabha at Guntur on 17 August 1918?
x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao presided; Pattabhi proposed an All-India Linguistic States Conference there.

s: On which date did Sir Vijayananda, president of the Andhra Mahasabha, meet Stafford Cripps?
x: Sir Vijayananda (1941-46) met Stafford Cripps on 2 April 1942.

s: At which Andhra Mahasabha session were the Ceded districts renamed Rayalaseema in 1928?
x: At the Nandyal session of 1928, on Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's proposal, the Ceded districts were named Rayalaseema.

s: Who presided over the Andhra Mahasabha session at Nandyal in 1928?
x: S. Radhakrishnan presided at Nandyal (1928); Gadicherla proposed the name Rayalaseema there.

s: Who presided over the fifth Andhra Mahasabha held at Nellore in 1917?
x: Konda Venkatappayya presided over the fifth session at Nellore on 1 June 1917.

s:
Match the following Andhra Mahasabha sessions with their presidents:
List-I (Session)
A. Vijayawada, 1914
B. Visakhapatnam, 1915
C. Nellore, 1917
D. Kadapa, 1918
List-II (President)
1. Konda Venkatappayya
2. Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao
3. Nyapati Subba Rao
4. Raja of Panagal
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Vijayawada 1914 - Nyapati Subba Rao; Visakhapatnam 1915 - Raja of Panagal; Nellore 1917 - Konda Venkatappayya; Kadapa 1918 - Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao.

s: Who presided over the sixth Andhra Mahasabha at Kadapa in 1918, where the province resolution was passed unanimously?
x: The sixth session at Kadapa in May 1918 was presided over by Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao and passed the province resolution unanimously.

s: Who presided over the women's session held along with the fourth Andhra Mahasabha at Kakinada in 1916?
x: At the Kakinada session of 1916 a women's session was held under Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi.

s: Who presided over the Special Andhra Sabha held at Madras in 1931, whose resolution was given to Gandhi for the Second Round Table Conference?
x: The Special Andhra Sabha at Madras in 1931 was presided over by Kadapa Koti Reddy; its resolution was handed to Gandhi for the 2nd RTC.

s: Who among the following initially opposed the Andhra demand in 1916 but later supported it at Cuddapah in 1918?
x: Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao of Cuddapah initially opposed the demand in 1916 but changed his position and supported it at Cuddapah in 1918.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Andhra movement between 1921 and 1935 is NOT correct?
o: Moderates such as Radhakrishnan, Sir Vijaya and C.R. Reddy kept the Mahasabha going.
The Congress in office in Madras had already completely taken over the demand in 1921.
The movement merged into Gandhian mass struggles.
The phase was described as ‘Swarajya within Swarajya’.
x: The Congress in office in Madras took over the demand from the declining Mahasabha only from 1946 onwards. The other statements correctly describe the 1921–1935 phase.

s: Who moved the separate-province resolution in 1917?
x: B.N. Sarma moved the separate-province resolution in 1917.

s: Who presided over the Congress session held at Kakinada in 1923?
x: Maulana Mohammed Ali presided over the Congress session held at Kakinada in 1923.

s: In which year did the Madras session block the Andhra resolution?
x: Madras blocked it in 1914, the provincial conference refused it in 1915, Lucknow took no decision in 1916 and a committee followed in 1918.

s: In 1931, the Andhra resolution was handed to Gandhi for the Second Round Table Conference. Who went to London to press it?
x: V.V. Jogayya Pantulu went to London in 1931, while Bobbili Raja and Mocherla Ramachandra Rao attended the Second Round Table Conference.

s: Who remarked, in connection with the 1918 resolution on linguistic provinces, that “the time has not come”?
x: Surendranath Banerjee stated that the time had not come for the proposed linguistic reorganisation.

s: On 6 February 1918, B. N. Sarma moved a resolution in the Imperial Legislative Council relating to which of the following?
x: B. N. Sarma moved the resolution for the creation of linguistic provinces in the Imperial Legislative Council on 6 February 1918.

s: What did the All-India Congress Committee do at Lucknow in 1916 when it examined the Andhra demand?
o: rejected the demand as harmful to national unity
referred the demand to the Montagu-Chelmsford Committee
examined the demand but took no decision
accepted the demand and immediately formed Andhra Province
x: The AICC examined the demand at Lucknow in 1916 but took no decision. Pattabhi Sitaramayya pressed the demand there with Tilak’s support.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the Nagpur Congress session of 1920?
o: The membership fee was reduced to four annas.
Provincial Congress Committees were reorganised on a linguistic basis.
An AICC of 350 members and a Congress Working Committee were provided for.
The goal of complete independence by armed means was adopted.
x: The Nagpur session changed the goal to Swaraj by peaceful and legitimate means, not complete independence through armed struggle. The other three features belonged to the reorganisation adopted at Nagpur.

s: Which of the following was a reason advanced by the Andhras for demanding a separate Congress circle in 1914?
o: The Simon Commission had recommended abolition of provincial committees.
Although 256 Andhra delegates attended the Madras Congress, none was placed on the Working Committee.
The Montagu declaration had excluded all Telugu-speaking areas.
The Andhra delegates were denied admission to the Congress session.
x: At the 1914 Madras Congress, 256 Andhra delegates attended, but no Andhra member was placed on the Working Committee. Tamils also blocked an Andhra resolution.

s: Where was the 1948 session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by Pattabhi Sitaramayya, held?
x: He presided at Jaipur in 1948; at Tripuri (1939) he had lost to Subhas Bose despite Gandhi's backing.

s: At which session were the Provincial Congress Committees reorganised on linguistic lines?
x: The Congress reorganised its Provincial Congress Committees on linguistic lines at the Nagpur session in 1920. Linguistic provinces had therefore been a Congress commitment since the 1920s.

s: In accordance with which of the following did the Nehru Report of 1928 advocate linguistic provinces?
x: The Nehru Report advocated linguistic provinces in line with the reorganisation of Provincial Congress Committees undertaken in 1920.

s: In which year was the Andhra Provincial Congress Committee formed?
x: The Andhra PCC was formed in 1918 and became a regular linguistic unit after the Nagpur session.

s: Which of the following correctly describes the Montagu-Chelmsford Report of July 1918?
o: It accepted the All-India Linguistic States Conference proposal.
It made no provision for Andhra.
It provided for a separate Andhra province.
x: The Montagu-Chelmsford Report of July 1918 made no provision for Andhra.

s: In which year did Ramadasu Pantulu move an Andhra state proposal in the Council of State?
x: Ramadasu Pantulu moved the Andhra state proposal in 1926; in 1925 he had amended Dr. Ramarao's resolution to seek linguistic states.

s: At which session did Pattabhi Sitaramayya lose the Congress presidential election to Subhas Chandra Bose?
x: Pattabhi lost at Tripuri in 1939 and later presided over the Jaipur session of 1948.

s: With which of the following is the AICC meeting at Bezawada in 1921 associated?
x: The AICC at Bezawada (1921) is linked with the Tilak Swaraj Fund.

s: On what basis did the Congress election manifesto of 1945-46 promise administrative units?
x: The 1945-46 manifesto promised units on a linguistic and cultural basis.

s: In 1938, which body assured the Andhra, Karnataka and Kerala deputation of linguistic redistribution?
x: The 1938 Wardha CWC gave this assurance.

s: What did Ramadasu Pantulu seek when he amended Dr. Ramarao's resolution in the Council of State in 1925?
x: Ramadasu Pantulu's 1925 amendment sought linguistic states; in 1926 he moved an Andhra state proposal.

s:
Consider the following statements about B.N. Sarma's 1918 resolution on linguistic provinces:
1. Jinnah opposed it.
2. K.V. Rangaswami Ayyangar supported it.
3. V.S. Srinivasa Sastri supported it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Rangaswami Ayyangar supported the resolution, while Jinnah and V.S. Srinivasa Sastri opposed it.

s: In which year was the Nehru Report that advocated linguistic provinces prepared?
x: The Nehru Report of 1928 backed linguistic provinces.

s: Who among the following supported B.N. Sarma's 1918 resolution?
x: K.V. Rangaswami Ayyangar supported it, while Jinnah and V.S. Srinivasa Sastri opposed it.

s: Of which body, formed on 22 January 1918, was Nyapati Subba Rao the first president?
x: The Andhra Congress Committee was formed on 22 January 1918 with Nyapati Subba Rao as first president and Konda Venkatappayya as first secretary.

s: Who was the first secretary of the Andhra Congress Committee formed in 1918?
x: Konda Venkatappayya was the first secretary; Nyapati Subba Rao was the first president.

s: With whose support was a separate Andhra Congress Committee approved at the Calcutta session of 1917?
x: The separate Andhra Congress circle was approved at Calcutta in 1917 with Tilak's support.

s: At which session was P. Anandacharlu, the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress, its President in 1891?
x: P. Anandacharlu presided over the Nagpur session of 1891, the first Telugu to be INC President.

s: Which Telugu leader was President of the Indian National Congress during 1960-62?
x: N. Sanjiva Reddy was INC President in 1960-62; Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided in 1948 at Jaipur.

s: To which party did the Raja of Bobbili, who opposed the separation of Andhra as Chief Minister of Madras, belong?
x: The Raja of Bobbili was the Justice Party Chief Minister of Madras from 1932 and opposed a separate Andhra.

s: Which two leaders wrote a pamphlet on linguistic provinces and circulated it among Congress leaders?
o: Nyapati Subba Rao and B.N. Sarma
Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao and Mutnuri Krishna Rao
x: Konda Venkatappayya and Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote a pamphlet on linguistic provinces for Congress leaders.

s: What did the Sri Bagh Pact primarily seek to do?
o: End the demand for a separate Andhra province
Establish Hyderabad as the permanent capital of Andhra
Allay Rayalaseema fears of Coastal Andhra domination
Create a separate university for Telangana
x: The pact was designed to remove Rayalaseema's fears of domination by Coastal Andhra and thereby facilitate a common Andhra demand.

s: On which date was the Sreebagh Pact concluded?
x: The Sreebagh Pact of 16 November 1937 put the capital and High Court in different regions and gave Rayalaseema first choice.

s: Besides Waltair, where did the Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 promise an Andhra University centre?
x: The Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 promised Andhra University centres at Waltair and Anantapur.

s: When the Sri Bagh Pact was implemented in 1953, Kurnool became the capital. Where was the High Court located?
x: When the pact was put into effect in 1953, Kurnool became the capital and Guntur the seat of the High Court.

s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Sri Bagh Pact?
o: Irrigation priority for Rayalaseema for ten years
Andhra University centres at Waltair and Anantapur
A cabinet ratio of 60:40 between Andhra and Telangana
x: The 60:40 cabinet ratio was a provision of the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956. The other provisions belonged to the Sri Bagh Pact.

s: For how many years did the Sri Bagh Pact give Rayalaseema priority in the Krishna, Tungabhadra and Pennar waters?
x: The Pact gave Rayalaseema irrigation priority for 10 years.

s: Under the Sri Bagh Pact, where were the capital and the High Court to be located?
o: In different regions, with Coastal Andhra choosing first
In different regions, with Rayalaseema choosing first
x: The Pact placed them in different regions, Rayalaseema choosing first; in 1953 Kurnool got the capital and Guntur the High Court.

s: Which of the following was a Rayalaseema signatory of the Sri Bagh Pact?
x: Kalluri Subba Rao signed for Rayalaseema with Kadapa Koti Reddy; the others signed for Coastal Andhra.

s: What was the name of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's residence in Madras, where Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema leaders signed a pact in 1937?
x: The 1937 pact was signed at Sri Bagh, Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house in Madras, and is named after it.

s: Which of the following was a Coastal Andhra signatory of the Sri Bagh Pact?
x: Prakasam signed for Coastal Andhra; Koti Reddy, Kalluri Subba Rao and Sitaram Reddy signed for Rayalaseema.

s: For which of the following did the Sri Bagh Pact later serve as a model?
x: The Sri Bagh Pact established a pattern of regional safeguards that was later used in the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956.

s: In which contemporary debates are the provisions of the Sri Bagh Pact particularly cited?
o: the status of the Telugu language in the Union List
the creation of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Council
the merger of Andhra with Maharashtra
Rayalaseema’s capital, High Court and irrigation concerns
x: The Sri Bagh terms concerning capital, High Court and irrigation remain important in Rayalaseema-related debates.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution, as it came into force on 26 January 1950, did not include a separate Andhra State.
2. Andhra State was formed before the Constitution came into force.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: There was no separate Andhra State in the Constitution of 26 January 1950; Andhra State was formed later, so statement 2 is wrong.

s: At which AICC session was the JVP Committee constituted in December 1948?
x: It was constituted at the Jaipur AICC session (December 1948) with Pattabhi Sitaramayya as president and reported in 1949.

s: What did the JVP Committee recommend regarding the creation of new provinces?
o: Creation of provinces solely on financial criteria
Postponement of the creation of new provinces
Merger of all Telugu areas with Hyderabad
Immediate creation of all provinces on a linguistic basis
x: The JVP Committee recommended postponing the creation of new provinces, while allowing Andhra's claim to be considered subject to giving up the claim to Madras city.

s: What did the Congress Working Committee recommend after the JVP report regarding the creation of Andhra State?
o: No linguistic state should be formed until after the States Reorganisation Commission.
Andhra should be merged with Rayalaseema and Hyderabad immediately.
Andhra should be formed without Madras city.
Andhra should be formed with Madras city as its capital and half the city shared with Tamil areas.
x: The Congress Working Committee recommended forming Andhra without Madras city. The Madras government and Tamil Nadu Congress accepted this position, while Andhra Congress wanted half of Madras town.

s: Which leader, and later Kamaraj, opposed sharing Madras city with the Andhras?
x: Rajaji and later Kamaraj opposed sharing Madras; the JVP formula required the Andhras to drop their claim to it.

s: The JVP Committee recommended that the demand for Andhra could be considered if the claim to which city was given up?
x: The JVP Committee stated that Andhra could be considered if its claim to Madras city was relinquished.

s: As Premier of Madras in 1937, C. Rajagopalachari:
o: included Rayalaseema in his cabinet and backed Andhra separation
left Rayalaseema out of his cabinet
x: Rajaji left Rayalaseema out of his cabinet as Premier in 1937 and later made anti-Andhra statements.

s: Which Andhra leader gave a separate report in the Madras Partition Committee?
x: T. Prakasam, champion of Andhra, gave a separate report; Kumaraswamy Raja chaired the committee.

s: In the Madras city question, what did the Andhra Congress claim?
x: The Andhra Congress claimed half of Madras town; Rajaji and later Kamaraj opposed any sharing.

s: Which Madras Chief Minister proposed the Cooum river as the boundary, with the part of Madras city north of it going to the Andhras?
x: The Raja of Panagal suggested the Cooum river as the boundary: north to the Andhras, south to the Tamils.

s: Who appointed the Dar Commission in June 1948?
x: It was appointed by the President of the Constituent Assembly in June 1948, with S.K. Dhar as chairman.

s: On what basis did the Dar Commission recommend that provinces should be reorganised?
x: The Dar Commission recommended administrative convenience rather than language as the primary basis for reorganisation.

s: What did the Dar Commission warn the creation of linguistic states could threaten?
x: The Commission warned that linguistic states threatened national unity and thereby rejected the linguistic basis at that stage.

s: During his 1948 visit to which city did Nehru promise a committee on the Andhra/linguistic province issue?
x: Nehru promised a committee during his 1948 Visakhapatnam visit, part of the background to the Dar Commission and JVP Committee.

s: After 1947, what did the Central Government mainly fear, which made it go slow on linguistic states?
o: a constitutional bar on language-based states
x: With Partition, Kashmir and the princely-state question still unsettled, the Government feared linguistic reorganisation could endanger national unity.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a member of the Linguistic Provinces Commission appointed in 1948?
x: The Commission consisted of S.K. Dhar, Dr Pannalal and Jagat Narayan Lal. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was a member of the later JVP Committee.

s: The general approach of which body did the JVP Committee's report reaffirm?
x: The JVP report reaffirmed the Dhar approach, putting security, unity and economic prosperity above immediate linguistic reorganisation.

s: With what was the committee formed by the Madras Government under Chief Minister P.S. Kumaraswami Raja primarily concerned?
o: Selecting the first Governor of Andhra State
Dividing the assets and liabilities between Madras and Andhra
Drafting a constitution for Andhra State
x: The committee was constituted to divide assets and liabilities between the proposed Andhra region and Madras. It failed because Madras leaders refused to surrender Madras city to Andhra.

s: Why is the formation of Andhra State in 1953 commonly described as the "Andhra exception"?
o: allowed Madras to become the capital of a separate Andhra State
created a state without any elected legislature
reversed the decision to use language as a basis for state formation
opened the way for the States Reorganisation Commission and nationwide linguistic reorganisation
x: Although the Dhar Commission and JVP Committee were cautious about linguistic states, the Andhra exception paved the way for the SRC and broader linguistic reorganisation.

s: On which date was the Draft Constitution, from which Andhra was dropped, published?
x: Andhra, first in the Draft's First Schedule, was omitted from the Draft of 21 February 1948 after Tamil and Kannada objections.

s: Apart from Jawaharlal Nehru and Vallabhbhai Patel, who was the third member of the JVP Committee?
x: The three members were Nehru, Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya; N. Sanjiva Reddy was not a member.

s: Who among the following was an Andhra member of the Madras Partition Committee of 1949?
x: The Andhra members were T. Prakasam, Kala Venkatrao, Bezawada Gopala Reddy and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy; the others named belonged to the Tamil side.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Dhar Commission:
1. It was appointed by the President of the Constituent Assembly.
2. It submitted its report on 10 December 1948.
3. It held language to be the main basis for reorganising provinces.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Appointed on 17 June 1948 by the President of the Constituent Assembly, it reported on 10 December 1948 in favour of administrative convenience, not language.

s: When did the JVP Committee submit its report?
x: Set up at Jaipur in December 1948, the JVP Committee reported in April 1949.

s: On which date did the Madras Partition Committee submit its report?
x: It reported on 4 January 1950; the plan to form the state by 26 January 1950 failed over Madras.

s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the JVP Committee?
x: The JVP Committee was Nehru, Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya; N. Sanjiva Reddy was not a member (APPSC 2021).

s: Which body, appointed by the Centre in December 1952, examined the financial and administrative implications of forming Andhra State?
x: The single-member Wanchoo Committee was appointed in December 1952 and reported on 7 February 1953. The Dhar Commission (1948) and JVP Committee (1948-49) dealt with linguistic states generally, and the Fazal Ali SRC (1953-55) with all-India reorganisation.

s: Who was the chairman of the Madras Partition Committee set up in December 1949?
x: Madras Chief Minister P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja chaired the Partition Committee; Prakasam, Gopala Reddy and Sanjiva Reddy were Andhra members.

s: Who was the chairman of the Linguistic Provinces Commission appointed in June 1948?
x: The Linguistic Provinces Commission was headed by Justice S.K. Dhar, with Dr. Panna Lal and Jagat Narayan Lal as members.

s: On which date did the President of the Constituent Assembly appoint the Dhar Commission?
x: The Dhar (Linguistic Provinces) Commission was appointed on 17 June 1948; it reported on 10 December 1948.

s: Which committee's report said, 'if public opinion is insistent and overwhelming, we as democrats have to submit'?
x: The JVP Committee (Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi), reporting in April 1949, said that democrats must submit to insistent and overwhelming public opinion.

s: The Visalandhra Mahasabha, formed in 1949, demanded a state comprising which areas?
o: The Telugu and Tamil-speaking areas jointly
x: The Visalandhra Mahasabha was formed to advocate the integration of all Telugu-speaking areas.

s: By which date did the Andhra Mahasabha demand that Andhra State be formed?
x: The Andhra Mahasabha demanded the formation of Andhra State by 26 January 1950.

s:
Consider the following statements about the mandate of the Dar Commission:
1. It was to examine the formation of a Gujarat province.
2. It was to examine the formation of Andhra and Karnataka.
3. It was to examine the formation of Kerala and Maharashtra, with their boundaries and consequences.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Dar Commission examined the formation of Andhra, Karnataka, Kerala and Maharashtra; Gujarat was not in its mandate.

s: Which of the following explains why the Andhra movement was repeatedly slowed before 1953?
o: The immediate acceptance of the Andhra demand by the Central Government
Leadership and regional splits, including Circars–Rayalaseema and Prakasam–Pattabhi divisions
The unanimous opposition of all Telugu-speaking districts to a separate state
The absence of any demand for linguistic organisation within Congress
x: Factional divisions between regions and leaders, notably Circars versus Rayalaseema and Prakasam versus Pattabhi, repeatedly weakened the movement.

s: Around 1910, Telugus formed about what share of the population of the Madras Presidency?
x: Telugus were about 40% (2 crore) of the Presidency, yet held only 8 high State jobs against 56 for non-Telugus.

s: In the Madras Presidency, how many Deputy Collector posts were held by Telugus?
x: Telugus held 21 Deputy Collector posts, 30 District Munsif posts and no District Judge posts; they held 8 high State jobs against 56 for non-Telugus.

s: Which of the following educational facilities was absent in Andhra in 1915?
x: In 1915, Andhra had no engineering, medical or law college, although it had 8 colleges and 163 secondary schools.

s: According to the Rayalaseema leadership, on which areas was the surplus revenue of the Andhra deltas mainly spent?
x: C is correct: a key revenue grievance was that surplus revenue from the Andhra deltas was allegedly spent on Tamil areas of the Madras Presidency.

s: Which districts were the most enthusiastic supporters of the demand for a separate Andhra province?
x: Krishna and Guntur were the most eager supporters of the demand for a separate Andhra province.

s: What did the separation of Bihar and Orissa in 1912 demonstrate?
o: The Madras Presidency could not be divided.
Provinces could be redrawn on linguistic lines.
Language had no role in territorial administration.
Only princely states could be reorganised.
x: The separation of Bihar and Orissa was cited as evidence that provincial boundaries could be redrawn on linguistic lines.

s: Which newspaper was described as the only daily from British Andhra?
x: Deshabhimani was an Anglo-Telugu paper from Guntur and was described as the only daily from British Andhra.

s: Who started the Andhra Patrika, founded in 1908 at Bombay and later shifted to Madras?
x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao founded Andhra Patrika at Bombay on 9 September 1908; it became a daily in 1914 and moved to Madras. Konda Venkatappayya founded Krishna Patrika (1902); Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao edited Swarajya (Vijayawada); Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham ran Desamata (Rajahmundry).

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Patrika – Popularisation of the word 'Andhra'
Andhra Advocate – The Andhra movement can serve national unity
Janmabhumi – Protection of Telugu culture through its own government
Deshabhimani – Propaganda by the Vizag district committee
x: Andhra Patrika popularised the word 'Andhra'. Deshabhimani argued for protecting Telugu culture through its own government, Andhra Advocate was used for propaganda and Janmabhumi linked the movement with national unity.

s: From where was Deshabhimani, the Anglo-Telugu paper that on 4 February 1910 called for a political meeting on Andhra problems, published?
x: Deshabhimani was published from Guntur, with editorials by Seshagirirao.

s: Who founded Krishna Patrika, started on 1 February 1902 as a voice of the Telugu districts?
x: Konda Venkatappayya (with Dasu Narayana Rao) co-founded Krishna Patrika in 1902, with Mutnuri Krishna Rao later as editor. Kasinathuni founded Andhra Patrika; Gadicherla edited Swarajya; Chilakamarti ran Desamata.

s: Replying to Tamil opposition, an Andhra Patrika writer argued that Tamils separating from Telugus would:
x: The Andhra Patrika writer argued that Tamils separating from Telugus would not harm national unity.

s: Along with a separate university, at which place did the early Andhra movement demand a port?
x: The university demand came with demands for agricultural and medical colleges and a port at Visakhapatnam.

s: The Swarajya associated with the Vandemataram era was published at Vijayawada, with which person as editor?
x: The Vijayawada Swarajya of the Vandemataram era had Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao as its editor.

s: Which book argued the Telugu claim over Madras by declaring that Madras was an Andhra city?
o: The Telugu People and Madras Presidency
On the Present Position of the Telugu People
x: Tanguturi Prakasam's book “Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae” argued that Madras was an Andhra city.

s: Where was Andhra Patrika originally founded?
x: Andhra Patrika was founded in Bombay, moved to Madras and became a daily in 1914.

s: Who founded Andhra Kesari at Rajahmundry in 1904 and wrote Andhrula Charitra?
x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao did both; Andhra Patrika is associated with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.

s: In the Madras Presidency around 1910, how many District Judge posts were held by Telugus?
x: Telugus held none of the District Judge posts, against 19 held by non-Telugus.

s: In 1915, how many of the 31 colleges of the Madras Presidency were in Andhra?
