x: Andhra had only 8 of the 31 colleges and 163 of 583 secondary schools in 1915.

s: Which of the following was NOT among the regions lukewarm towards the separate Andhra demand?
x: Guntur, with Krishna, was the keenest supporter; Rayalaseema, Nellore and Ganjam were lukewarm and saw it as a Circars movement.

s: On which date was the separation of Bihar from Bengal announced at the Delhi Durbar?
x: Bihar's separation was announced at the Delhi Durbar on 12 December 1911; the Bihar and Orissa province began on 1 April 1912.

s: What is Andhra Patrika credited with popularising?
x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's Andhra Patrika popularised the word 'Andhra'.

s: With whom was Desamata of Rajahmundry associated?
x: Desamata (Rajahmundry) was Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham's paper; Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao ran Andhra Kesari.

s: In which newspaper did Jonnavittula Gurunatham publish his 1911 series of articles 'On the present position of the Telugu people'?
x: Gurunatham of Guntur wrote six articles on the position of the Telugu people in The Hindu in 1911.

s: How many articles did Jonnavittula Gurunatham write in The Hindu in 1911 on the present position of the Telugu people?
x: He wrote a series of six articles in The Hindu in 1911.

s: Who wrote “Maa Telugu Talliki,” recognised as the State song of Andhra Pradesh?
x: “Maa Telugu Talliki” was written by Sankarambadi Sundarachari and is the State song of Andhra Pradesh.

s: At which Andhra Mahasabha session was the demand for a separate university for the Telugu people first raised?
x: The separate-university demand was first raised at the first session at Bapatla in 1913, because Madras University neglected Telugu; Vijayawada (1914) only reiterated it.

s: Who introduced the Andhra University Bill on 20 August 1925?
x: Education Minister A.P. Patro of the Justice Party introduced the Andhra University Bill on 20 August 1925.

s: Who drafted the Andhra University Bill?
x: Kattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy drafted the Andhra University Bill.

s: On which date was Andhra University inaugurated at Waltair?
x: After Subbaroyan's ministry fixed the seat at Visakhapatnam (December 1928), it was inaugurated at Waltair on 5 September 1930.

s: What was the main reason for C.R. Reddy's choice of Waltair as the university seat?
o: Political importance and proximity to Madras
x: C.R. Reddy chose Waltair for its climate and setting. He also coined the expression “City of Destiny” for Visakhapatnam.

s: When an amendment excluded Rayalaseema from Andhra University's jurisdiction, to which university did its colleges go back?
x: The amendment excluded Rayalaseema from Andhra University's jurisdiction, and its colleges returned to Madras University.

s: Which of the following cultural markers is correctly matched with its date or period?
x: Waltair Andhra Varotsavalu took place in December 1937. Andhra Abhyudaya Dinam was observed on Ugadi, 24 March 1936; Diwali 1937 was marked as Andhra State Day; the Telugu-medium resolution dates to 1915.

s:
Consider the following statements about universities:
1. Osmania University was established in 1918.
2. Sri Venkateswara University, Tirupathi, was established in 1954.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Osmania University dates from 1918 and Sri Venkateswara University from 1954; Andhra University was set up in 1926.

s: Which university was founded in 1954 in answer to Rayalaseema's grievance at exclusion from Andhra University?
x: Sri Venkateswara University at Tirupati was founded in 1954, answering Rayalaseema's grievance after it had been excluded from Andhra University.

s: In which year did the Madras government first appoint a committee on the Andhra University question?
x: A Madras government committee came in 1921; the Bill followed in 1925.

s: Whose ministry chose Visakhapatnam as the seat of Andhra University in December 1928?
x: Subbaroyan's ministry chose Visakhapatnam in December 1928; the Act of 1925 came under the Raja of Panagal's Justice Party government.

s: During which period was S. Radhakrishnan Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University?
x: Radhakrishnan served 1931-36, between C.R. Reddy's two terms (1926-31 and 1936-49).

s: What did C.R. Reddy, who recommended Waltair for Andhra University, call Visakhapatnam?
x: C.R. Reddy named Visakhapatnam the 'City of Destiny'; the Guntur Youngmen's Literary Association is the 'cradle'.

s: Where was the first headquarters of Andhra University when it was established in 1926?
x: Andhra University began in 1926 with its headquarters at Vijayawada (Bezawada); it moved to Waltair, Visakhapatnam, in 1930.

s: Which university was established on 26 April 1926 as the first university for the Telugus?
x: Andhra University, set up under the 1925 Act, was established on 26 April 1926 and is the oldest university in today's AP.

s: Which of the following towns was NOT among the rival claimants for the seat of Andhra University before Visakhapatnam was chosen in 1928?
x: Vijayawada, Rajahmundry and Anantapur claimed the seat; Kurnool was not a claimant.

s: How much money was set aside in Andhra University's centenary year 2026 to push it into the global top 100?
x: For its centenary in 2026, Rs 500 crore was set aside to push Andhra University into the global top 100.

s: Who designed the emblem of Andhra University?
x: The Andhra University emblem, a rising sun, was designed by Kowta Rammohan Sastri with the guidance of C.R. (Cattamanchi Ramalinga) Reddy.

s: After which year did Konda Venkatappayya come to prominence among the Andhra Moderates?
x: Konda Venkatappayya rose among Andhra Moderates after 1908, so he was not an Andhra delegate at the first INC session of 1885.

s: Who was known as 'Andhra Ratna'?
x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya was 'Andhra Ratna'; 'Deshabhakta' was Konda Venkatappayya.

s: Who had the title 'Desoddharaka'?
x: Desoddharaka is Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, not Pattabhi.

s: Which of the following pairs (title – person) is correctly matched?
x: Deshabhakta is Konda Venkatappayya; Desoddharaka is Kasinathuni, Andhra Kesari is Prakasam and Andhra Ratna is Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah.

s: Which leader did Mutnuri Krishna Rao, editor of Krishna Patrika, invite to Andhra in 1907?
x: Mutnuri Krishna Rao invited Bipin Chandra Pal in 1907.

s: Who led the first salt squad in Madras in 1930?
x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao led the first salt squad in Madras (1930).

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gokhale of South India — Mocherla Ramachandra Rao
x: Desoddharaka was the title of Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, not Pattabhi Sitaramayya.

s: Of which town did Tanguturi Prakasam become municipal chairman at the age of 31?
x: Tanguturi Prakasam became the municipal chairman of Rajahmundry at 31.

s: Which volunteer corps did Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah organise in 1921?
x: Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah ('Andhra Ratna') organised the Ramadandu ('Rama's army') in 1921 during the Chirala-Perala movement.

s: With which movement of 1921 is Duggirala Gopalakrishnaiah's Ramadandu associated?
x: Ramadandu worked in the Chirala-Perala movement of 1921, when people refused municipal taxes and moved out to Ramanagar.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

A. First Widow Remarriage in Andhra
B. First Andhra Mahasabha
C. Sribagh Agreement
D. Formation of Andhra State
x: The first widow remarriage in Andhra was in 1881, the first Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla in 1913, the Sribagh Agreement in 1937 and the formation of Andhra State in 1953, giving A, B, C, D.

s:
Consider the following statements about the chronology of the Andhra State movement:
1. The Dhar Commission came before the formation of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
2. Swami Sitaram's fast came after the formation of the Visalandhra Mahasabha.
3. The States Reorganisation Commission was set up after Swami Sitaram's fast.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The order was Dhar Commission (1948), Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949), Swami Sitaram's fast (1951) and the SRC (December 1953), so all three are correct.

s: Gandhi visited Hyderabad on 9 March of which year?
x: Gandhi's Hyderabad visit was on 9 March 1934, the same year as the first Rayalaseema Mahasabha (28 January).

s: Where was the first widow remarriage in Andhra held on 11 December 1881?
x: The first widow remarriage in Andhra took place at Rajahmundry on 11 December 1881.

s: At which place did the first Rayalaseema Mahasabha (28 January 1934) demand a separate university?
x: Presided over by Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao, it opposed inclusion in Andhra University and demanded a separate university at Tirupati.

s: Where did the Nizam Andhra Mahasabha, distinct from the Andhra Mahasabha of the Madras Presidency, begin in 1930?
x: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha began at Jogipet in 1930 under Suravaram Pratapa Reddy; the Madras Presidency body began at Bapatla in 1913 under B.N. Sarma.

s: Who led the Andhra Jana Sangham, formed in Hyderabad in 1921 and later renamed the Andhra Mahasabha?
x: Madapati Hanumantha Rao led the Andhra Jana Sangham, later restructured as the Andhra Mahasabha.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rayalaseema Mahasabha?
o: The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha was presided over by Nemali Pattabhirama Rao.
The First Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held at Madras in January 1934.
The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha was held at Kadapa in 1935.
The Second Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposed a separate Andhra state.
x: Nemali Pattabhirama Rao presided over the first Rayalaseema Mahasabha at Madras (28 January 1934), not the second. The second session, at Kadapa in September 1935, was presided over by T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy and opposed a separate Andhra state.

s: What was the main fear behind the opposition of R. Suryanarayana Rao and N.M. Sastry in 1938?
x: The new Rayalaseema Mahasabha leaders R. Suryanarayana Rao and N.M. Sastry opposed the demand because they feared Circars domination.

s: The second Rayalaseema Mahasabha, held in September 1935, adopted which of the following resolutions?
o: Opposition to a separate Andhra state
Demand for immediate merger with Telangana
Demand for a separate Andhra province without safeguards
Demand for Madras as the capital of Andhra State
x: The second Rayalaseema Mahasabha held at Kadapa in September 1935 opposed the creation of a separate Andhra state.

s: To which of the following did the 1935 opposition of the Rayalaseema Mahasabha to a separate Andhra state eventually contribute?
x: The 1935 resolution opposing a separate Andhra state led to the Sri Bagh Pact, which addressed Rayalaseema safeguards.

s: What position did the Rayalaseema Mahasabha communicate to the Dhar Commission in 1948?
o: A united Andhra province with Vijayawada as capital
Immediate merger with the Hyderabad State
A separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as capital
Continuation of the Madras Presidency without reorganisation
x: In 1948, the Rayalaseema Mahasabha told the Dhar Commission that it wanted a separate Rayalaseema state with Madras as its capital.

s: Who presided over the second session of the Vishalandhra Mahasabha, held at Hyderabad in 1954?
x: K.V. Ranga Reddy presided over the 1954 session; Swamy Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Vishalandhra.

s: Who founded the Jatiya Mahasabha Andhra?
o: Madapati Hanumantha Rao and B.N. Sharma
Ravi Narayana Reddy and K. Subrahmanyam
Suravaram Pratapa Reddy and Burgula Ramakrishna Rao
Konda Venkatappayya and Nemali Pattabhirama Rao
x: Suravaram Pratapa Reddy and Burgula Ramakrishna Rao founded the Jatiya Andhra Mahasabha. Madapati Hanumantha Rao led the Andhra Jana Sangham (1921), and Ravi Narayana Reddy led the Communists at Bhongir (1944).

s:
Assertion (A): The Communist faction took control of the main Andhra Mahasabha at the historic 11th Bhongir Session in 1944.
Reason (R): The session was presided over by the communist leader Ravi Narayana Reddy.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Ravi Narayana Reddy presided at the 1944 Bhongir session, but the Communist takeover came from their wider support among delegates, not from his chairing the session.

s: Who presided over the first Rayalaseema Mahasabha (Madras, 28 January 1934)?
x: Nemali Pattabhirama Rao presided; S. Satyamurti opened the session.

s: In 1933, Kadapa Koti Reddy wanted which city as the capital of Andhra?
x: Kadapa Koti Reddy (1933) wanted Madras as the Andhra capital.

s: Where did the New Rayalaseema Mahasabha of 1938 hold its first session?
x: Its first session was at Adoni; R. Suryanarayana Rao and N.M. Sastry of Bellary led it.

s: Of which organisation's first session, held at Jogipet in 1930, was Suravaram Pratapa Reddy the president?
x: The Nizam Andhra Mahasabha began at Jogipet (Medak) in 1930 under Suravaram Pratapa Reddy.

s: Who presided over the second Rayalaseema Mahasabha held at Kadapa in September 1935?
x: The second Rayalaseema Mahasabha at Kadapa (1935) under T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy opposed a separate Andhra state.

s: Under whose leadership did the Communists take control of the Andhra Mahasabha at the 11th Bhongir session of 1944?
x: At the 11th Bhongir session (1944), the Communists led by Ravi Narayana Reddy took control of the Andhra Mahasabha.

s:
Consider the following statements about Nehru's announcement of 25 March 1953:
1. Madras was ruled out as the capital of Andhra State.
2. The capital had to be located within Andhra.
3. Some offices could continue in Madras for a period.
Which of the above statements are correct?
x: Nehru's 25 March 1953 decision rejected Madras as capital and required a capital within Andhra, while allowing some offices to continue in Madras for a period.

s: Before which date did Nehru say the temporary capital of Andhra State was to be decided?
x: Nehru's 25 March 1953 statement wanted the temporary capital fixed before 1 July 1953.

s: Which town was the temporary capital of Andhra State?
x: Kurnool was the temporary capital; Guntur got the High Court.

s: In which year were the members of the first Andhra State Assembly elected to the Madras Assembly?
x: The Assembly was made up of those elected to the Madras Assembly in 1952.

s: What was the nature of the legislature of Andhra State at its formation?
o: A regional committee of the Madras Assembly
x: Andhra State had an Assembly but no Legislative Council.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Rayadurg taluk went to Andhra and was included in Anantapur district. Adoni and Alur went to Kurnool district, while Bellary, Hospet and the other listed areas went to Mysore.

s: Where was the Andhra High Court established in 1954?
x: The Andhra High Court was set up at Guntur in 1954; the Madras High Court retained jurisdiction until then.

s: Which court kept jurisdiction over Andhra until the Andhra High Court was set up at Guntur in 1954?
x: The Madras High Court kept jurisdiction in the interim.

s: Of which High Court was Justice Mishra, who inquired into the Bellary question, the Chief Justice?
x: Mishra was Chief Justice of the Hyderabad High Court; Wanchoo was of Rajasthan.

s: Which of the following Bellary areas did NOT go to Mysore?
x: Adoni (with Alur) went to Kurnool district of Andhra; Siruguppa, Hospet and Sandur went to Mysore.

s: Which of the following pairs (Bellary area – where it went) is correctly matched?
x: Bellary taluk went to Mysore on the Mishra report; Rayadurg went to Anantapur and Adoni and Alur to Kurnool.

s: On whose report was the decision to assign Bellary taluk to Mysore based?
o: Kumaraswamy Raja, Chairman of the Partition Committee
M. Trivedi, Special Officer of Andhra State
Justice Mishra, Chief Justice of the Hyderabad High Court
Justice Wanchoo, Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
x: Bellary taluk was assigned to Mysore on the basis of Justice Mishra’s report. Justice Mishra was the Chief Justice of the Hyderabad High Court.

s: Who chaired the Partition Committee (1949–50) on administrative arrangements for a new Andhra State?
x: The 1949–50 Partition Committee was chaired by Madras Chief Minister Kumaraswamy Raja.

s: When was the Wanchoo Committee appointed?
x: It was appointed in December 1952, after Nehru's statement of 19 December, and reported on 7 February 1953.

s: On which date did Nehru announce the Centre's decisions on the Wanchoo report?
x: 25 March 1953 was Nehru's decision statement; 7 February 1953 was the report itself.

s: What was the number of the Andhra State Act, 1953, which received assent on 14 September 1953?
x: The Andhra State Act was Act 30 of 1953.

s: On which date did the Wanchoo Committee submit its report?
x: Appointed in December 1952, the single-member Wanchoo Committee submitted its report on 7 February 1953; Nehru announced the Centre's decisions on 25 March 1953.

s: With which of the following did the Wanchoo Committee (1953) deal?
o: Determining the permanent capital of India
Reorganisation of all Indian states on linguistic lines
Boundaries, finances, assets and administration of the new Andhra State
x: Its terms covered boundary division, financial settlement, asset distribution and administrative arrangements, not the capital of India.

s: How many members did the Wanchoo Committee have?
x: It was a single-member committee of Justice K.N. Wanchoo.

s: Of which High Court was Justice Kailas Nath Wanchoo then the Chief Justice?
x: Wanchoo was Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court; Justice Mishra of the Hyderabad High Court handled Bellary.

s: Which of the following was NOT among the Wanchoo Committee's terms of reference?
x: Wanchoo looked at boundaries, financial settlement, division of assets and administrative arrangements of Andhra, not the capital of India.

s: Who was the Centre's Special Officer for setting up Andhra State?
x: C.M. Trivedi was the Special Officer, and later the Governor.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Wanchoo Committee?
o: It recommended that the Andhra Government work temporarily from Kurnool for three to five years.
Its member was the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court.
It dealt with the financial and administrative implications of the new state.
x: Wanchoo recommended that the Andhra Government work temporarily from Madras city, not Kurnool, for three to five years, as Andhra lacked capital infrastructure.

s:
Consider the following statements about Madras city and the new Andhra State:
1. Wanchoo recommended that the Andhra Government work temporarily from Madras for 3-5 years.
2. Nehru accepted Wanchoo's Madras recommendation.
3. The JVP Committee made Andhra conditional on Telugus giving up their claim to Madras.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Wanchoo's Madras recommendation was not accepted; Nehru said there was no question of Madras as capital. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

s: Which of the following describes the financial and administrative position of the newly formed Andhra State?
o: It had no need for an asset division with residual Madras.
It possessed a developed capital and a major commercial centre.
It was administratively and economically orphaned, lacking a developed capital and commercial centre.
It had inherited the entire financial surplus of residual Madras.
x: The new state lacked both developed capital infrastructure and a commercial centre and was described as administratively and economically orphaned.

s: In which of the following was the Wanchoo apportionment of assets and liabilities largely reproduced?
o: The schedule of the Andhra State Act, 1953
x: The Act's schedule largely reproduced Wanchoo's apportionment of assets and liabilities.

s: Nehru's statement of 25 March 1953 left which matters to be considered separately later?
o: The capital and the High Court
x: Services and financial implications were left for later consideration.

s: Between Andhra and which of the following were the assets and administration of Madras State divided?
x: Assets were divided between Andhra and residual Madras.

s: Which committee handled the allocation of employees in the 2014 bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The Kamalanathan Committee dealt with employees, the Sheela Bhide Committee with Schedule IX institutions and the Section 6 committee with the capital.

s: Which committee handled the Schedule IX institutions in the 2014 bifurcation?
x: Sheela Bhide dealt with Schedule IX institutions; Kamalanathan dealt with employees.

s: In the 2014 bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, under which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act was an expert committee set up on the new capital?
x: The Section 6 committee studied the capital for residual Andhra Pradesh in 2014, a parallel to the 1953 capital question.

s: The Sreebagh Pact of 1937 promised priority for irrigation in Rayalaseema and Nellore on which rivers?
o: Krishna, Godavari and Pennar only in coastal Andhra
x: The Sreebagh Pact promised priority for irrigation in Rayalaseema and Nellore on the Tungabhadra, Krishna and Penna for ten years or as needed.

s: Under which of the following was the Tungabhadra Board set up for the works shared by Andhra and Mysore after Bellary was divided?
x: The Tungabhadra Board was established under the Andhra State Act, 1953 to manage the shared works.

s: After Bellary's division, between Andhra and which state were the Tungabhadra works shared?
x: The works were shared by Andhra and Mysore, under the Tungabhadra Board.

s: How many new gates of the Tungabhadra dam were opened on 26 June 2026?
x: C.R. Patil opened 33 new gates with the three Chief Ministers.

s: For how many years did the Sreebagh Pact of 1937 give Rayalaseema and Nellore priority for irrigation on the Tungabhadra, Krishna and Penna?
x: The Sreebagh Pact gave Rayalaseema and Nellore irrigation priority for 10 years or as long as needed.

s: Which Union Minister opened 33 new gates of the Tungabhadra dam on 26 June 2026?
x: On 26 June 2026, Union Minister C.R. Patil opened 33 new gates of the Tungabhadra dam with the three Chief Ministers.
